data: Dockets 25-0677 / 25-0679 (cons.) — ComEd LDPAC tariff Final Order
ICC approves ComEd's large-demand project tariff with a 50 MW deposit threshold; the order is now on appeal

The currently binding security-deposit and cost-allocation framework for large-load interconnection in ComEd territory, with a parallel investigation running in 26-0364. Deposit figures come from secondary reporting, not the order text.
Project 58481 — PUCT proposal for publication of 16 TAC 25.194

Docket 59475 — Oncor and LCRA TSC Bell County East to Big Hill 765-kV CCN
Oncor's joint 765-kV transmission CCN is contested by a landowner and environmental coalition citing data-centre load growth
A delay or denial would constrain transmission capacity in a corridor directly tied to ERCOT large-load growth. The docket carries 6,577 filings.
Docket ER-2026-0143 — Evergy Missouri Large Load Power Service rate design
Evergy's Missouri rate case includes a contested Large Load Power Service design for data centres as an LPS subclass

Determines whether data centres get a bespoke rate class in Evergy's Missouri territory, setting the pricing template for future deals. Sourced from search snippets; the docket page exceeded output limits.
Oncor identifies at least 38 GW of large load meeting RTP criteria for its 2026 filing

The filter between 226 GW of raw queue and 38 GW of RTP-qualifying load is the single most useful conversion datapoint in ERCOT. Non-data-centre load alone would raise peak demand ~60%. ~77% of the base capital plan is growth-attributable.
Louisiana bill would bar household rate increases caused by data-centre demand at 50 MW and above
Non-passage leaves Entergy Louisiana ratepayers exposed to cost pass-through from the Meta project absent a statutory backstop.
Docket 26-EKCE-110-CON — Order O-003737 approving the special-contract Energy Supply Agreement between Evergy Kansas Central and Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America
The KCC approved a unanimous settlement and the Evergy/Panasonic special-contract energy supply agreement for the De Soto battery plant

The only Evergy Kansas large-load customer contract actually approved inside the window, and the template any data-centre ESA will be measured against: 10-year term, minimum-bill provisions the Utilities Director called the most robust he had reviewed, substantial collateral, and discounts confined to base rates with nothing off the fuel, property-tax or transmission riders.
Evergy signs first four ESAs under its new large load tariff, ~1.9 GW aggregate, naming Beale Infrastructure, Google and Meta

Tier 1 signed and active load of ~2.4 GW against a 10+ GW Tier 2. Evergy is the only tracked utility that names counterparties against specific jurisdictions. Missouri Senate Bill 4 also extends PISA to 2035 and allows CWIP recovery for new gas.

Committed load already exceeds half the system peak. These three figures stay unchanged across all three quarters, which is itself notable — APS is not converting its uncommitted pipeline.
Dominion Energy Q4 2025 earnings call slides
Dominion Energy Virginia's December 2025 contracted-capacity ladder was SELOA 27.4 GW, CLOA 11.0 GW and ESA 10.2 GW, about 48.5 GW in total

Confirms at source the December 2025 CLOA of 11.0 GW and ESA of 10.2 GW that the tracker had taken second-hand from a Q2 2026 history slide; no correction needed. The quarter converted +0.4 GW into ESA and +2.0 GW into CLOA while SELOA fell 0.8 GW as engineering-stage capacity moved up the ladder. Customer quality: 82% investment grade.
PPL advanced-stage data centres reach 25.2 GW, up 23% from 20.5 GW in one quarter

PPL's ESAs require data-centre customers to pay ~80% of anticipated load until service-extension costs are recovered — one of the more protective structures disclosed. Kentucky queue holds a further 9.3 GW through 2032.
Southern reports 10 GW contracted across 26 projects against a 75+ GW prospective pipeline

Pipeline grew from 50 GW to 75+ GW year on year while contracted rose 6 to 10 GW. Southern publishes explicit stage definitions, making it the cleanest comparator in the coverage set. Capital plan up 30% to $81B.

Docket X-37921 — LPSC Large Load Additions Non-Binding Guidelines
LPSC publishes a twelve-part checklist utilities must address for large-load requests

Labelled non-binding, but the document itself states that failing to address the criteria places risk on the utility — effectively a soft-law standard every Louisiana large-load contract will be measured against. Docket number from a search snippet, not independently fetched.

Ameren Q4 2025 full-year results and guidance presentation
Ameren announced 2.2 GW of executed Missouri large-load ESAs against a 3.4 GW Missouri construction-agreement funnel inclusive of those ESAs, plus 850 MW in Illinois

Ameren's first disclosed ESA execution and the origin of the series. The deck does NOT state a standalone construction-agreement-without-ESA figure, only the inclusive 3.4 GW total, so that cell is not-stated rather than the arithmetic 1.2 GW residual. The Missouri large-load rate plan approved 2025-11-24 applies at 75 MW with a 12-year term and 80% minimum demand.
Docket 24-0508-EL-ATA — AEP Ohio Schedule DCT correspondence on modifications
AEP Ohio's data-centre tariff remains under active administration while on appeal to the Ohio Supreme Court
Tariff terms are still moving even with the appeal pending in S.C. 2025-1458 — counterparties should not treat Schedule DCT as frozen.

Case PUR-2026-00011 — application for approval of large-load connection queue process standards
Virginia Electric and Power Company filed its large-load connection queue process standards as directed by the November 2025 final order in PUR-2025-00058

The rulebook governing how Dominion evaluates and sequences transmission delivery-point requests from distribution companies serving data centres. Respondents include Google, Amazon, Microsoft, STACK, Tract, Verrus, CloudHQ, Emerald AI and the Data Center Coalition, so the outcome sets queue position, study timelines and transparency for essentially every large Virginia site.
Docketed 2026-02-19; hearing held 28-30 April 2026; awaiting decision
Commission order, then a Dominion compliance filing
Docket 26-0075-E-CN — application for a CPCN for the West Virginia portions of the MidAtlantic Resiliency Link 500 kV project
NextEra Energy Transmission MidAtlantic applied for a CPCN for the West Virginia segments of MARL, a 107.5-mile 500 kV line of which about 58.9 miles sit in West Virginia

MARL is the principal new 500 kV import path into the West Virginia and northern Virginia corridor. Its approval timing and routing bear directly on deliverability and interconnection headroom for large loads sited in eastern West Virginia and the adjacent PJM zones.
Heavily contested; Staff motion to toll or dismiss denied 2026-09-04
Evidentiary hearing 26 Oct - 2 Nov 2026; decision due 2027-03-06
CAISO Large Load Considerations issue paper
CAISO opens its Large Loads Initiative covering interconnection, co-location, transmission service and cost allocation

Explicitly cites FERC's PJM co-location order as a model CAISO may adopt — evidence the PJM framework is migrating west. California Energy Commission forecasts CAISO data-centre load up 1.8 GW by 2030 and 4.9 GW by 2040.
PJM Board decisional letter closing the Critical Issue Fast Path on large load additions
PJM adopts Bring-Your-Own-New-Generation with an Expedited Interconnection Track, and Connect-and-Manage for loads that do not

This is the choice a PJM data-centre developer now faces: bring your own generation for priority service, or accept curtailment ahead of pre-emergency demand response. Large load addition is defined at 50 MW at a single point of interconnection; the expedited track is capped at 10 projects a year with a $500,000 non-refundable study deposit.
KCC Utilities Division update to the House Energy Committee summarising Docket 25-EKME-315-TAR, the Evergy Large Load Power Service tariff
KCC's Director of Utilities set out the full approved terms of Evergy's Large Load Power Service tariff to the Kansas House energy committee

The most complete official statement of what a Kansas data centre actually faces: 75 MW threshold, 12-year base term plus up to 5-year ramp, 80% take-or-pay minimum bill, collateral up to two years of minimum bills, 36-month termination notice, and base demand rates set 50% above the standard Industrial and Large Power rate with all-in bills 8-10% higher. A Bring Your Own Generation path preserves the SB-98 sales-tax exemption.
Tariff approved 2025-11-06; docket still shown Open
GRDA board of directors agenda, 14 January 2026 — item 4.b, power purchase agreement with five SMT OKC entities
GRDA's board took up approval of a power purchase agreement with SMT OKC II, III, V, VI and VII LLC

GRDA is adding contracted third-party supply alongside its own build programme, which is the capacity pool any new large load in its footprint draws against. Volume, term and price are not disclosed in the agenda.
Board action item; outcome not published
Docket ER26-247 — SPP High Impact Large Load (HILL) and HILLGA study process
FERC accepts SPP's HILL framework, the first RTO process integrating transmission, generation and load interconnection studies for large loads
Creates a defined 90-day study-and-approval track for large loads paired with generation, materially shortening the diligence timeline for co-located generation deals in SPP.
Oncor transmission interconnection queue reaches 226 GW, of which 210 GW is data centres
Against a current system peak of 31 GW. The queue is more than seven times the peak. Transmission expansion projects are costed at $32-35B, including $10B of 765-kV import paths.
